title: Compact tool handshake and SDK cognitive load playbook
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight, opinionated approach to the tool-call handshake plus SDK ergonomics with the explicit goal of minimizing developer cognitive load while preserving the guarantees we need for production (idempotency, observability, partial results).

Problem statement (short):
Teams building on Hosted API repeatedly struggle with two coupled problems: 1) complex multi-message handshakes between the model stream and client-side tool adapters that leak implementation surface and increase bugs, and 2) SDK surfaces that force app developers to reason about streaming internals, rehydration, and partial structured output mechanics. The result: slow integrations, brittle tool handling, and scattered telemetry.

Design goals (non-negotiable):
- Low cognitive load: SDK should offer a single, small set of primitives for the 80% case (call tool, receive result, recover).
- Progressive commitment: avoid heavyweight two-phase commits unless the client explicitly opts-in; default to optimistic, restartable micro-transactions.
- Stream-first semantics: support partial/streamed tool outputs with deterministic reassembly at the SDK boundary.
- Strong observability: every tool invocation must carry a minimal trace header and be correlated to token offsets and session ids.
- Safe defaults: idempotency tokens, timeouts, and automatic fallbacks to safe text responses when structured output fails.

High-level proposal summary:
1) Compact handshake frame: introduce a single short JSON envelope (ToolFrame) embedded in the model stream for tool intent + metadata and a matching ToolResultFrame for results. The envelope is intentionally small and machine-friendly: {"tool": "<name>", "id": "<id>", "mode": "sync|async|prefetch", "spec": "<schema-ref>"}.
2) SDK primitives: expose two main primitives in official SDKs: callTool(toolName, args, options) -> StreamingHandle and onToolResult(handle, callback) -> deterministic reassembly. Helpers: callToolSync (await final structured result), callToolOptimistic (fire-and-forget metadata-only).
3) Graceful structured-degradation: a single, well-documented fallback flow: if parsing/validation fails at the SDK boundary, the SDK returns a textual fallback and an error tag. Developers can opt into strict mode to escalate as exceptions.
4) Telemetry contract: every ToolFrame issued by the model must include trace_id, tool_id, and token_offset_start. The SDK auto-attaches client-side trace info and surface-level metrics: time-to-first-byte, validation-latency, bytes-streamed.

Why this is different from prior designs:
- Condensed envelope reduces back-and-forth: avoids session-level handshakes, instead uses idempotency and small metadata to coordinate replay and resume.
- SDK-centric reassembly and validation: pushes the parsing burden to the SDK, not to the app developer. This reduces repeated parsing logic in customers and ensures consistent validation rules across clients.
- Progressive commitment allows speculative optimization (prefetch, optimistic tool resolution) without full transaction semantics.

Detailed mechanics (flow examples):
A) Sync tool call (common):
- App calls callToolSync("search", {q: "llm inference"})
- SDK emits a client-side invocation envelope (client_trace, idempotency_token) along the request metadata and maps the expected schema id.
- Model outputs a ToolFrame in the stream: {"tool": "search", "id": "tk-1234", "mode": "sync", "spec": "schema://search-result/v1"} then streams payload frames (raw JSON lines) and finally a ToolResultFrame with status.
- SDK assembles payload frames, validates against spec, returns typed object to app. If validation fails, SDK returns fallback_text + error metadata.

B) Async tool call with resume:
- callTool(..., options={mode: 'async'}) returns StreamingHandle immediately.
- Server-side execution may be long; partial results flush as payload frames. If connection drops, the SDK resumes by reconnecting and re-attaching to same idempotency_token and token offsets; the server replays from last-acked offset.

Idempotency and replay rules (short):
- Every client invocation must contain an idempotency_token (UUID) and optional last_seen_offset.
- Server guarantees at-least-once delivery for payload frames; SDK deduplicates on frame sequence numbers + id.
- Side-effects: recommend a single linearizable mode for tool executions that cause external side-effects (capture in options.side_effect: 'confirmed'|'best-effort'), default 'best-effort'.

SDK ergonomics and API surface (concrete):
- callTool(toolName: string, args: object, opts?: object): StreamingHandle (simple object with .on('data'), .on('end'), .cancel())
- callToolSync(tool, args, opts) -> Promise<{result: object|string, metadata: {status, elapsed_ms, validation}}>
- callToolOptimistic(tool, args) -> {ticket: string} (sends intent but returns immediately; result delivered as event later)
- SDK config: validationMode: 'lenient'|'strict' (default lenient), resumeStrategy: 'auto'|'manual', telemetrySampler: number (0..1)

Observability and incident post-mortem checklist:
- Correlate trace_id across model frames, SDK events, and any backend tool executions.
- For partial outputs, record the token_offset range and which frames failed validation.
- When structured validation fails > threshold per session, alert product-team for model/tool contract drift.

Operational considerations and rollout plan (phased):
Phase 0 - Labs (now): ship experimental SDK helpers in JS + Python as opt-in. Monitor: validation failure rate, resume success rate, mean TTFB for tool frames.
Phase 1 - Beta (4–8 weeks): hardened envelope and default idempotency token; add telemetry sampling hooks and automatic dedupe on SDK. Invite 3 partner customers.
Phase 2 - GA (after Beta signals): enable compact handshake by default on hosted-api; publish SDK migration guide and compatibility notes; provide a lightweight server-side simulator in the SDK for local testing.

Backward compatibility and migration notes:
- Existing clients that expect ad-hoc JSON in the stream continue to function when we set an opt-in header (X-Rd-Compact-Handshake: true). We will not switch default until Beta is complete.
- Provide a compatibility shim that maps old frames to ToolFrame envelope for older SDKs.

Open questions / risks (explicit):
- Schema discovery: how and where to host authoritative schema specs? (Confluence vs. model catalog vs. schema registry)
- Side-effect semantics: we currently recommend 'best-effort' default but some customers will require strong guarantees; need pricing/SLAs if we support linearizable side-effects.
- Edge clients and unstable networks: resume safety relies on precise offsets — need a small experiment to verify cross-region resume behavior.

Next steps / immediate TODOs:
- Engineering: prototype ToolFrame encoding and minimal server-side router that supports idempotency_token and replay endpoints. (Owner: Samir)
- SDK: ship JS helper with callToolSync and optimistic call primitives behind an experimental flag. (Owner: Jordan)
- Product: finalize validationMode semantics and write a short migration guide for customers with toolside integrations. (Owner: Ava)
- Observability: define 5 core metrics and dashboards (tools.per_minute, tool.validation_failure_rate, tool.resume_success_rate, tool.latency_p50/p95, tool.bytes_streamed_per_call).

Appendix: quick example payloads (toy)
- ToolFrame (model->client):
  {"tool":"search","id":"tk-1234","mode":"sync","spec":"schema://search-result/v1","meta":{"token_offset_start":123}}
- Payload frames (streamed lines):
  {"type":"payload","seq":1, "data":"{\"hits\":[]}"}
  {"type":"payload","seq":2, "data":"{\"cursor\": "c-1"}"}
- ToolResultFrame:
  {"type":"result","id":"tk-1234","status":"ok","elapsed_ms":132}

Notes to reviewers (short):
- Look for places where we implicitly push complexity onto customers; call those out.
- Prefer concrete SDK method names and failure modes rather than abstract promises.
- If you have a major scenario that requires two-phase commit for tool side-effects, please document it in the linked JIRA ticket.

End.
